title: Mitigate KV shadow-eviction oscillation causing transient throughput collapse
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Incident summary: During a customer-facing capacity event on 2026-02-15 we observed a rapid, self-amplifying oscillation in prefix KV cache evictions that coincided with a 3x increase in tail latency and a temporary throughput collapse across multiple host pools. Unlike classic eviction storms, this behavior was driven by a feedback loop between per-prefix hotness estimation and our eviction scorer: aggressive per-prefix demotion caused hot prefixes to lose cached state, which increased request work and then re-marked them as hot, triggering re-insertion and subsequent demotion again — a thrash pattern we call 'shadow eviction oscillation'.

Why this is unique: existing eviction guardrails protect against global eviction storms and TTL replay; this incident exposes instability when a small number of prefixes have bursty, uneven traffic and the scorer uses short-lived histograms without hysteresis. The runtime's continuous-batch pipeline and KV slab allocator amplified the oscillation by compacting/freeing slabs in ways that increased allocation latency under load.
actions: A1 - Short-term: Add eviction scorer hysteresis + smoothing (Mateo) - implement exponential moving average on per-prefix hotness and require sustained delta > 30% over 10s before demotion - due 2026-03-02
A2 - Short-term: Deploy emergency config to increase min-retention for prefixes flagged as 'recently-hot' from 1s to 15s (on-call) - rollout window 2026-02-20 to 2026-03-01
A3 - Mid-term: Introduce 'eviction-backoff' that delays eviction for prefixes experiencing >2 re-insert cycles within 60s (SLA-safe) - owner: Kira Thompson - due 2026-03-12
A4 - Mid-term: Add slab-level allocation telemetry and correlate with per-prefix eviction/reinsert rate - owner: Priyanka Singh - due 2026-03-08

A5 - Long-term: Implement canary and chaos test that reproduces prefix-hotness oscillation patterns against dedicated test cluster; include synthetic workloads and failure injection - owner: Eng Reliability - due 2026-04-01
A6 - Runbook: Update prefixcache runbook with detection playbook, automated rollback flag, and mitigation toggle endpoints - owner: SRE Docs - due 2026-03-05
A7 - Post-deploy verification: Create dashboard and alerting for 'prefix reinsert rate' and 'eviction oscillation score' with pager thresholds - owner: Observability - due 2026-03-06
acceptance_criteria: Eviction hysteresis deployed to canary pool without increased error rate for 48h
Dashboard panels show stable prefix reinsert rate under synthetic burst tests (<1 reinsert cycle per prefix per minute)
No customer-facing latency spikes attributable to eviction cycles for 7 days post-deploy
Runbook contains a clear detection query and a one-click mitigation toggle
updates: 2026-02-18: Ticket opened after on-call postmortem. Initial hypothesis captured and short-term config toggle applied to one pool. Mateo assigned as owner.

2026-02-20: Emergency config increased min-retention for recently-hot prefixes in two pools; observed 40% reduction in reinsert cycles but isolated allocation latency persisted. Telemetry gaps noted for slab-level visibility.
2026-02-24: PoC for EMA smoothing committed (branch: feature/kv-ema-hysteresis). Benchmarks locally show reduced oscillation in synthetic workloads. Preparing PR for review.
2026-03-01: PR opened (github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1987). Kira added design doc link and suggested backoff thresholds. Scheduling canary deploy for 2026-03-04.
2026-03-05: Canary deployed to 10% of traffic in eu-west; preliminary telemetry looks promising: per-prefix reinsert cycles dropped 65% on canary nodes. Monitoring for side-effects continues.
comments: PM review - Jonah Park (2026-02-19): Agree with short-term toggle. Need to confirm customer impact window and notify affected customers via status page.
Design feedback - Lena Ortiz (2026-02-22): EMA smoothing looks good; consider cap so very-hot prefixes still get priority. Also add a demo script for load pattern reproduction.
SRE note - Carlos Mendes (2026-02-28): Observed slab compaction spikes on hosts with high fragmentation. Adding slab metrics to telemetry is high priority.
Security note - Priya Verma (2026-03-03): No secrets or policy changes. Ensure mitigation toggles respect RBAC for SRE and Eng only.
